I have watched both of those videos...about 5 times each. I am fascinated with kinks, and on the journey to finding why some bounce price and some do not. I have a few theories that I am currently testing.

One of those theories involves the difference between the following two pictures... I may be wrong, but when price engulfs the source of the engulf (to the upside) a retest of the kink would be confirmation of a swap zone. But...as we know...they don't always react.

Continued from above -

This becomes important when price crosses back up through the FL, and comes back down later on. Some bounces inside the FL will look like engulfs when they are actually fakeouts. One of the main differences for this may be situations where the FTR/Kink consumes the orders in the source of the engulf as opposed to situations where the kink/FTR does not RT far enough to consume the orders in the source of the engulf. In this scenario, a FO to the source might occur.

("A" is the source of the topside engulf)

I am convinced the nuances will work themselves out with more practice. The answers will be found after hundreds of hours of screen time.

I will be spending a significant amount of time in the coming days analyzing swap zone kink bounces. The longer I trade, the more I am convinced trading is all about watching 'footsteps' of price as it moves from FL to FL and decision to decision.

Price leaves hints along the way...just like an animal leave footprints as it travels through the forest. Slowing down and training my eyes to follow these footsteps is the key to understanding future price movement.

It is hard to do..and takes a tremendous amount of time to refine this skill.

Training my eyes to ONLY see what they need to see.

USD- JPY: Practice

Good example of a failure - price does not bounce at the green FTR.

If we look a bit closer ant the overall context of price, it is obvious why a long was a bad idea.

Let's start with the Chart:

Why the failure? Well price is coming from a FO to MPL - which is a reached target for Buyers with no PA giving us an engulf. Don't buy when price is coming from a reached target for Buyers. We need PA in the form of an engulf with a valid (unmet) target.

Why a failure?

Because price was coming from a reached target for buyers. Price hits MPL with no PA engulfing to the upside.

It is amazing how many bad trades can be avoided by simply looking to the left and seeing if price has already consumed MPL or if it has been engulfed...

I have been dealing with a major point of confusion for a while...maybe someone here knows the answer?

After watching IF's videos multiple times I am practicing finding nicely hidden LS kinks for price to bounce. The problem: in the video IF says we must use the entire candle that crosses the 'kink' if there is no LTF data available to refine the actual entry.

I identify the correct LS and Kink...I always drop down to a 1-min chart to find the best 'refined' kink...the last place where price crosses the kink. Price often time ends up bouncing within the larger TF kink but misses the highly refined kink. How do we know where to place our stop loss and entry? The kink size changes depending on the TF.

Here is a good example on USD-JPY:

Here is the HTF:

The following charts shows the kink based on the time frame: As you can see, I would have missed the trade entirely if I had used the 1-min kink. the 5 -min kink was perfect. How do we know which one to choose? I think this is a hugely important to question to answer...
